m: Increasing heart rate always increases cardiac output.
fix: At very high rates diastolic filling time falls, so stroke volume and cardiac output can drop.

m: The first heart sound is caused by closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves.
fix: S1 is mitral and tricuspid closure at the start of systole; S2 is aortic and pulmonary closure.

m: The T wave represents atrial repolarisation.
fix: The T wave is ventricular repolarisation; atrial repolarisation is hidden in the QRS complex.

m: Mean arterial pressure is the average of systolic and diastolic pressure.
fix: Because diastole lasts longer, MAP is approximately diastolic plus one-third of pulse pressure.

m: Halving the radius of a vessel halves the flow through it.
fix: By Poiseuille's law flow varies with the fourth power of radius, so halving the radius cuts flow about sixteen-fold.

m: Most carbon dioxide is carried in blood bound to haemoglobin.
fix: Most CO2 (about 70%) is carried as bicarbonate; smaller amounts are carbamino compounds and dissolved gas.

m: A right shift of the oxygen dissociation curve means haemoglobin holds oxygen more tightly.
fix: A right shift (raised CO2, H+, temperature, 2,3-BPG) lowers affinity and releases more oxygen to tissues.

m: Carbon monoxide poisoning lowers the measured arterial PaO2.
fix: PaO2 is often normal; CO blocks oxygen carriage by haemoglobin, so pulse oximetry and PaO2 can mislead.

m: Low oxygen is the main normal drive to breathe.
fix: Arterial CO2 (via central chemoreceptors) is the main normal drive; hypoxic drive matters mainly in hypoxaemia.

m: A reduced FEV1 always means obstructive lung disease.
fix: FEV1 falls in both patterns; the FEV1/FVC ratio is low in obstruction and normal or high in restriction.

m: Most filtered water is reabsorbed in the collecting duct.
fix: About two-thirds is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule; the collecting duct fine-tunes reabsorption under ADH.

c: Renal regulation of fluid, electrolytes and acid-base
m: Aldosterone acts mainly to retain water.
fix: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium and H+ secretion; ADH mainly regulates water.

m: Curare blocks acetylcholine release.
fix: Curare competitively blocks nicotinic receptors at the end-plate; botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release.

m: The resting membrane potential is mainly due to sodium.
fix: It is mainly due to potassium leak through open K+ channels, maintained by the Na+/K+ pump.

m: T4 is the main active thyroid hormone in tissues.
fix: T4 is mainly a prohormone; it is converted to the more active T3 in peripheral tissues.

m: Glucagon and insulin are secreted by the same cells.
fix: Insulin comes from beta cells and glucagon from alpha cells of the islets.

m: Ovulation occurs on day 14 in every woman.
fix: The luteal phase is relatively fixed (about 14 days); ovulation timing varies with cycle length.

m: Bleeding time tests the coagulation factors.
fix: Bleeding time reflects platelet function and vessel response; PT and aPTT test coagulation factors.

m: A person with blood group O can receive blood from any group.
fix: Group O individuals have anti-A and anti-B antibodies; group O is the universal red cell donor, AB the universal recipient.

m: A normal pH excludes an acid-base disorder.
fix: Mixed disorders or full compensation can give a normal pH; check bicarbonate, PaCO2 and anion gap.

m: Compensation fully corrects pH in chronic acid-base disorders.
fix: Compensation is usually incomplete; overcorrection suggests a second primary disorder.

m: A competitive inhibitor lowers Vmax.
fix: Competitive inhibitors raise Km without changing Vmax; non-competitive inhibitors lower Vmax.

m: HbA1c reflects blood glucose over the previous week.
fix: HbA1c reflects average glucose over about 2–3 months, and is unreliable in haemolysis and haemoglobinopathies.

m: HDL carries cholesterol from the liver to tissues.
fix: HDL mediates reverse cholesterol transport from tissues to the liver; LDL delivers cholesterol to tissues.

m: Large doses of fat-soluble vitamins are harmless because excess is excreted.
fix: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) accumulate and can cause toxicity.

m: Glucose in the urine is a reliable test for diagnosing diabetes.
fix: Glycosuria depends on the renal threshold; diagnosis uses plasma glucose or HbA1c.

m: Kwashiorkor and marasmus are both defined by severe wasting.
fix: Oedema is the hallmark of kwashiorkor; marasmus is severe wasting without oedema.

m: All porphyrias cause skin photosensitivity.
fix: Acute intermittent porphyria causes neurovisceral attacks without photosensitivity.

c: Inborn errors of amino acid metabolism
m: Phenylketonuria is treated by removing phenylalanine completely from the diet.
fix: Phenylalanine is essential; it is restricted, not eliminated, and tyrosine becomes essential.

m: A positive PCR always means live, active infection.
fix: PCR detects nucleic acid, which can persist after the organism is dead or the infection is cleared.
